segments.text: When a bank lends you money, it doesn't hand you someone else's savings.
Meet Maya. She walks into her bank and asks for a ten-thousand-dollar loan.
The bank checks her credit, approves the loan, and writes two new lines in its ledger.
On one side, an asset: Maya's promise to repay. On the other, a deposit.
And with a few keystrokes, ten thousand dollars appears in her account.
No vault was opened. That money did not exist before. The loan created it.
